children: President Donald Trump said he plans to remove a 10% tariff on Irish whiskey, which was part of the duties imposed on most European Union goods that included wine and spirits.

"Everybody's been bugging me about this one thing: 'Would you do me a favor? It's so unfair what's going on. Could you possibly take the tariffs off of Irish whiskey?'" Trump said during the Irish Open golf tournament on Sunday.
"On behalf of the United States of America, I am going to take the tariffs off," he announced.
Trump made a similar concession in April after King Charles' state visit, when the president lifted certain tariffs on UK whiskey – including Scotch and spirits made in Northern Ireland.
Chris Swonger, CEO of the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, said Trump's move to lift Irish whiskey tariffs is another positive step toward reducing barriers to spirits trade.
"As U.S. hospitality businesses enter the critical holiday season, this action will provide a welcome boost for retailers, restaurants, consumers and the American economy," Swonger said.

"Nothing exemplifies the U.S.-Ireland trade relationship better than Irish whiskey," said Eoin Ó Catháin, director of the Irish Whiskey Association, noting that exports to the U.S. were worth €450M ($520M) in 2025.
"We will continue to work with our EU and U.S. counterparts to secure a return to the zero-for-zero arrangement for all drinks exports," he added.
Companies that own Irish whiskey brands include Pernod Ricard

title: Trump to lift 10% tariff on Irish whiskey
